headline: Rose's two-out double in the ninth beats the Mets
recap: The Phillies beat the Mets 4-3 at home. The score was tied 3-3 after the top of the seventh, and Philadelphia won it in the bottom of the ninth. Luis Aguayo singled leading off, moved up on a sacrifice bunt, and scored from second on Pete Rose's two-out double to right field.

Marty Bystrom started for the Phillies and went 6.2 innings, allowing three earned runs with six strikeouts and two walks. Scott Holman started for the Mets and pitched six innings, allowing three runs. The Phillies scored all three of those runs in the sixth, and New York answered with two in the seventh to tie it.

Stan Bahnsen followed Bystrom, struck out three over 1.1 hitless innings, and Porfi Altamirano retired the side in the ninth for the win. Rose finished 2 for 3 with a walk and an RBI. Pat Zachry took the loss for the Mets.
